items.title: 67296_Chauncey Morehouse oral history interview
items.q: A drummer with Major Bowes on the Sunday Morning Capitol Theater Family, Morehouse has played drum specialties several times

ctx.x: Daily Press, Saturday, March 25, 1939. Obviously that other article from the newspaper called the Press is the same one, the same newspaper, Long Island Daily Press. This one is entitled "Chauncey Morehouse of Forest Hills collects Weird Drums". The subtitle is - has 14 tuned to different pitches upon which tunes can be played. And the article reads: Remember those travelogues you saw in the movies where wild savages played weird tomtoms. You saw the savages but the drums you heard were probably played in a…

N'goma is a single drum shaped like a giant egg cup, large at the top and small at the bottom with skins on each end. The Africans dance right on the drum at tribal jam sessions, beating out the rhythm as they dance. Morehouse's drums open up a new field to the musician. The instruments do not replace ordinary ones or the tympany but represent a new musical instrument. By using different types of sticks, Morehouse achieves different effects from Boleros and Rhumbas to oriental tones. Morehouse is enthusiastic…

foreign drums, he is rapidly becoming one. He admits that although it didn't start as a hobby, his collection is proving so engrossing, it is rapidly becoming one. Piece by piece, he has collected an unusual set of drums from foreign countries. One of them is a clay drum shaped like a vase from Turkey. When he uses it in radio work, he can make it double for an African drum. "In Turkey," Morehouse explained, "the drum is really a duet instrument and is played with a three string mandolin.
